I am an empirically oriented sociologist whose research focuses on **social inequality and social structure**, particularly in relation to migration, trust, and social cohesion.

My work uses international comparative quantitative approaches to examine how inequalities shape individual life chances, institutional access, and broader social relationships. More recently, my research has also addressed child and youth wellbeing, health inequalities, disability, and the development of research infrastructure for comparative social research.

Alongside my research, I have extensive experience in university teaching in social stratification, social inequality, political and macro sociology, comparative methods, statistics, and applied data analysis. I approach quantitative methods as tools for answering substantive sociological questions and place particular emphasis on helping students develop practical and transferable empirical research skills.
